{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-in-s","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"74ce5b3020b77e051fc0cca9d3fb8e111701fe7c439742789aca483bf83e1e98","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-in-class-std:lineage:14","source_registry_sha256":"2800087d52ca58455ac6dac735a6e1bd60a4442f9e09c2356d96bd9ed8102504","source_liveness_sha256":"4d2b75b9a10fb774f53fb2d906a3a7a7f75f5e9387f8b4ddcd423e9b7828d59b"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Credential indicators, watercraft, parking placards, and renewing, amending or replacing a credential","heading":"C — Organ donor and military indicators, watercraft operation, disability parking placards, credential expiration and renewal, late-renewal testing, military renewal, address and name amendments, and replacements","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Organ donor and military indicators, watercraft operation, disability parking placards, credential expiration and renewal, late-renewal testing, military renewal, address and name amendments, and replacements
Knowledge domain: what can be added to an Indiana credential and how to keep it current — the organ donor heart and military indicators, when a license is needed to run a boat, how disability parking placards are issued and expire, when credentials expire, what late renewal costs and requires, and the deadlines for reporting address and name changes or replacing a lost card.

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
Choosing to be an organ donor puts a small heart on the front of your credential. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Under Indiana's Donor Choice Law, a person aged 18 or older can declare the wish to be an organ donor, and family members cannot override that choice at death. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
A person under 18 can declare the wish to donate only with a parent's or legal guardian's permission, and that adult must consent to donation when the minor dies. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
An active-duty member of the US Armed Forces can add an active-duty indicator by showing a current Common Access Card (CAC) at a branch during a new issuance or renewal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A01
A veteran who was not dishonorably discharged can add a veteran indicator by providing a Department of Defense DD 214 that verifies the discharge. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A01
A surviving spouse of a deceased veteran can add a veteran spouse indicator by presenting proof of the veteran's discharge or separation, the marriage certificate and the veteran's death certificate. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A01
Anyone operating a watercraft whose engine produces more than 10 horsepower must carry a valid driver's license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A01
A person aged 15 or older without a driver's license may operate such a watercraft only after finishing a boater education course that the Indiana Department of Natural Resources has approved, and must carry a valid Indiana ID card while doing so. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A02
Nobody younger than 15 may operate a watercraft with an engine of more than 10 horsepower. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A02
A person whose driver's license is suspended may not operate a watercraft, and reckless or intoxicated boating or breaking watercraft laws can add points to the driver record. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A02
On Indiana boundary waters, Indiana residents operating a watercraft must carry an Indiana driver's license, while residents of other states need one only on an embayment, river or stream in Indiana. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A02
A disability parking placard is available to people with a permanent or temporary disability, to people issued or eligible for a Disabled Hoosier Veteran plate, and to organizations providing transportation or facilities for people with physical disabilities. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A02
To apply, a health care provider (for example a physician, chiropractor, podiatrist, physician's assistant, advanced practice registered nurse, optometrist or ophthalmologist) completes State Form 42070, which can be taken to any branch or mailed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A02
No health care provider certification is needed for a person who has received or is eligible for a Disabled Hoosier Veteran plate. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A02
A permanent placard is free and does not expire unless a provider certifies the disability is no longer permanent or the Indiana Department of Veteran Affairs certifies the holder is no longer a Disabled Hoosier Veteran. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A02
A temporary placard carries a fee and expires on the provider's stated date or one year after issue, whichever comes first. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A02
A placard issued to an organization expires on January 1 of the fourth year after the issue year, or earlier if it stops running programs or facilities for people with disabilities. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A02
Using an expired placard can lead to a fine, and parking in the diagonally striped area beside a reserved space is never allowed, even with a valid placard. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A03
A person who loses a credential while temporarily living outside Indiana may be able to get an interim credential. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A03
If your name and residential address have not changed, you may be eligible to renew or replace online at myBMV.com, and online or BMV Connect kiosk renewal is allowed every other renewal. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A03
A probationary license expires at 21 years and 30 days and may be renewed online if the holder qualifies, while all other credentials expire at midnight on the holder's birthday. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A03
If your birthday falls on a day when branches are closed, the credential expires at midnight on the next business day. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A03
Everyone who renews a credential after its expiration date is subject to an administrative penalty. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A03
Renewing a license expired for at least 180 days but not more than five years requires the administrative penalty, a knowledge exam and a standard vision screening. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A03
Renewing a license expired for five years or more requires the administrative penalty plus a knowledge exam, a driving skills exam and a standard vision screening. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A03
US citizens and permanent lawful residents can renew a license or ID card up to 24 months before it expires, while people with lawful temporary status can renew only up to 30 days ahead. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A03
A learner's permit can be renewed up to 30 days before it expires. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A03
A driver aged 21 or older with six or more active points must pass the knowledge exam to renew the license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A03
A license held by someone serving outside Indiana with the US Armed Forces stays valid for 90 days after discharge, post-deployment or the end of the out-of-state service residence. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A03
To renew an expired license after discharge, a veteran visits a branch with Department of Defense proof of discharge or the long form DD 214, and can add the veteran indicator at that visit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A04
After legally changing personal information you must amend your credential, which can be done at any BMV branch. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A04
A change of principal (legal) address must be reported and an amended credential applied for within 30 days, in person at a branch with Appendix A documents. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F33 | anchor: A04
A mailing address can be changed online at myBMV.com, at a BMV Connect kiosk or at a branch. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F34 | anchor: A04
For a name change, update Social Security records first, wait at least one business day, then visit a branch within 30 days of the change with Appendix A documents to amend the credential. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F35 | anchor: A04
A lost or stolen credential can be replaced through myBMV.com or a BMV Connect kiosk when the name and residential address are unchanged, up to 10 online replacements before a branch visit is required. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F36 | anchor: A04
If anything other than the mailing address has changed, a replacement cannot be ordered online; the holder must amend the credential at a branch within 30 days with Appendix A documents. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

Misconceptions: a valid placard does not allow parking in the striped access aisle; most credentials expire on the birthday, not on the issue anniversary; a late renewal brings a penalty even when no exam is required; a mailing address change does not update the principal address, which needs a branch visit.
Mnemonics: thirty days to report a move or a name change; renew up to twenty-four months early as a citizen, thirty days as a temporary resident; ten horsepower and fifteen years for boats.
Glossary: indicator means a marker printed on a credential such as the donor heart or a military symbol; principal address means the legal residence address; interim credential means a temporary credential issued while living outside Indiana; administrative penalty means the charge for renewing after expiration; Disabled Hoosier Veteran plate means the Indiana license plate for qualifying disabled veterans.
Dynamic facts: placard fees, State Form numbers, myBMV.com and kiosk services, the BMV phone line and the online replacement limit can change; confirm them on IN.gov/BMV.
